title: Related Party Transactions - Audit Procedures
exam_relevance: MODERATELY TESTED - Expect 2-4 questions on CPA AUD exam about identifying related parties, required procedures, disclosure requirements, and fraud risks. Also tested on FAR for accounting treatment.
learning_objectives: Understand what constitutes a related party relationship
Know required procedures for identifying related parties
Understand audit procedures for related party transactions
Recognize fraud risks associated with related parties
Evaluate business rationale and economic substance of transactions
Know disclosure requirements for related party transactions
Understand management representations regarding related parties

introduction.why_important: Related party transactions require special audit attention because: (1) they may not be at arm's length (fair market terms), (2) they can be used to manipulate financial results, (3) they present fraud risks, and (4) extensive disclosure is required.

key_standards.accounting: ASC 850 (Related Party Disclosures) - accounting and disclosure requirements

introduction.exam_importance: Know how to identify related parties, required procedures (especially inquiries), and disclosure requirements.

definition_of_related_parties.general_definition: Related parties are persons or entities that have the ability to control or significantly influence the management or operating policies of another entity, or entities under common control.

common_types_of_related_parties.affiliates: Parent companies, subsidiaries, entities under common control
common_types_of_related_parties.principal_owners: Individuals or entities that own >10% of voting interests
common_types_of_related_parties.management: Officers, directors, executives, and their immediate families
common_types_of_related_parties.entities_managed_by_related_parties: Entities where management or principal owners have control or significant influence
common_types_of_related_parties.other: Trusts for benefit of employees (pension funds), employee benefit plans

examples: Company and another company where CEO owns 25% interest
Company and joint venture where company has significant influence
not_related_parties: Two companies just because they have common customers/suppliers
Two companies just because they're in same industry
Economic dependence alone (major customer) - not related party unless also have control/influence
definition_of_related_parties.exam_note: Related party = control or significant influence. Economic dependence alone is NOT sufficient.

not_arms_length.issue: Related party transactions may NOT be conducted at arm's length (fair market value terms)
examples: Parent sells assets to subsidiary at inflated prices to shift profits
Company leases building from CEO at below-market rent as indirect compensation
Company sells inventory to related entity at low price to reduce reported income
not_arms_length.audit_concern: Transactions may not reflect economic reality or fair value

earnings_management.issue: Related party transactions can be used to manipulate earnings
examples: Company sells assets to related party at gain to boost earnings
Company purchases services from related party at inflated prices to reduce earnings (tax avoidance)
Timing of transactions manipulated to achieve desired results

fraud_risk.issue: Related party transactions present fraud risk, particularly for fraudulent financial reporting
schemes: Recording fictitious revenue through sales to related parties (who don't actually pay)
Concealing liabilities through related party arrangements
Creating appearance of liquidity through circular transactions
Hiding assets or income in related entity
fraud_risk.exam_emphasis: Related parties are specifically identified as fraud risk in AU-C 240

disclosure_requirements.issue: Extensive disclosure required - failure to disclose is GAAP violation

required_audit_procedures.description: Auditor must perform specific procedures to identify related parties and transactions.

inquiries: Identity of related parties and changes from prior period
Whether entity entered into transactions with related parties
Type, purpose, and terms of transactions
inquiries_with_management.exam_note: Inquiry with management is PRIMARY method for identifying related parties

procedures_to_identify_related_parties.inquire_with_governance: Inquire with those charged with governance about related party relationships
procedures_to_identify_related_parties.inquire_with_predecessor: If initial audit, inquire with predecessor auditor about related parties

review_records.description: Review entity's procedures for identifying and accounting for related parties
review_specific_records: SEC filings and proxy statements (public companies)
Conflict of interest statements from management
Records of transactions requiring board/management approval

inspect_records_for_names.description: During the audit, be alert for names indicating related parties

procedures_to_identify_related_parties.review_confirmations: Review confirmations from banks and attorneys for indication of related parties (guarantees, co-borrowers, etc.)
procedures_to_identify_related_parties.confirm_with_registrar: For public companies, confirm with stock registrar or transfer agent

procedures_for_identified_transactions.description: Once related party transactions are identified, perform specific procedures:

inspect_underlying_documents.procedure: Inspect invoices, contracts, agreements, and other documentation for terms

inquire_about_business_purpose.procedure: Inquire with management about business purpose and rationale
inquire_about_business_purpose.key_question: Why was this transaction entered into? What business purpose does it serve?
inquire_about_business_purpose.red_flag: No clear business purpose or purpose doesn't make economic sense

procedures_for_identified_transactions.evaluate_accounting: Evaluate whether transaction is properly accounted for and disclosed per ASC 850

test_for_proper_authorization.who_should_approve: Board of directors, audit committee, or other appropriate level based on company policy
test_for_proper_authorization.concern: Related party transactions may bypass normal controls

procedures_for_identified_transactions.confirm_terms_with_related_party: Consider confirming terms and amounts with related party (though less reliable than independent third party)
procedures_for_identified_transactions.evaluate_effect_on_financial_statements: Assess whether transaction materially affects FS and whether disclosures are adequate

specific_concern_identified_previously_u.situation: If auditor identifies related party transactions that management did NOT previously disclose
required_actions: Inquire with management WHY relationship/transaction wasn't disclosed initially
Perform additional procedures to identify other transactions with that party or other undisclosed related parties
Assess implications for audit and risk assessment
specific_concern_identified_previously_u.exam_emphasis: Finding undisclosed related party is RED FLAG - raises fraud risk and questions about management integrity

evaluating_business_rationale.description: Critical procedure: Evaluate whether transaction has business rationale beyond just relationship

understanding_business_rationale.requirement: For SIGNIFICANT related party transactions, understand and evaluate the business rationale
questions_to_ask: What is the business purpose of this transaction?
Why was it conducted with related party rather than independent third party?
Does the transaction make economic sense?
Is there a legitimate business need being met?

indicators_of_questionable_transactions.no_apparent_business_purpose: Transaction has no clear business rationale
indicators_of_questionable_transactions.unusual_terms: Terms significantly different from market terms with no explanation
indicators_of_questionable_transactions.lacks_economic_substance: Transaction has form but no economic substance (assets go in circle)
indicators_of_questionable_transactions.inconsistent_with_strategy: Transaction doesn't fit entity's business strategy or operations
indicators_of_questionable_transactions.concealment_attempts: Transaction not properly documented or disclosed

red_flag_examples: Company sells asset to related party at significant gain, then leases asset back at above-market rates (earnings manipulation)
Company and related party engage in offsetting transactions that net to zero (circular transactions to create appearance of activity)
Company purchases consulting services from related party at inflated prices with no clear deliverables
Related party transactions occur only at period-end (timing manipulation)

implications: May lack economic substance - question whether transaction should be recorded
May need to evaluate whether transaction violates laws/regulations
if_no_clear_business_purpose.auditor_response: Perform additional procedures, apply professional skepticism, consider implications for audit opinion

significant_unusual_transactions.description: Management override procedures (from fraud standards) require evaluation of significant unusual transactions - many involve related parties
significant_unusual_transactions.definition: Significant transactions outside normal course of business or that appear unusual given auditor's understanding
significant_unusual_transactions.overlap_with_related_parties: Many significant unusual transactions involve related parties
required_evaluation: Evaluate whether transaction is overly complex
Consider whether designed to achieve specific accounting result
Assess whether terms are at arm's length
significant_unusual_transactions.exam_connection: This ties to management override fraud risk - significant unusual related party transactions require special scrutiny

disclosure_requirements.description: ASC 850 requires extensive disclosure of related party transactions

required_disclosures_per_asc_850.nature_of_relationship: Must disclose the nature of the related party relationship
required_disclosures_per_asc_850.description_of_transactions: Describe the transactions, including normal recurring and non-recurring transactions
required_disclosures_per_asc_850.dollar_amounts: Disclose dollar amounts of transactions for each period FS presented
required_disclosures_per_asc_850.amounts_due: Disclose amounts due to or from related parties, including terms
required_disclosures_per_asc_850.separate_disclosure_for_material: Material related party transactions should be separately disclosed, not aggregated

arm_s_length_representation.rule: FS CANNOT represent that related party transactions were at arm's length UNLESS this can be SUBSTANTIATED
arm_s_length_representation.rationale: Cannot claim transactions were at market terms without evidence
arm_s_length_representation.auditor_evaluation: If FS claim arm's length, auditor must obtain evidence supporting the claim

control_relationship_disclosure.requirement: If control relationship exists, must be disclosed even if NO transactions occurred
control_relationship_disclosure.example: Parent-subsidiary relationship must be disclosed even if no intercompany transactions during year

disclosure_requirements.auditor_responsibility: Auditor must evaluate whether disclosures are ADEQUATE per ASC 850. Inadequate disclosure is GAAP departure requiring modified opinion.

management_representations.requirement: Auditor must obtain written representations from management about related parties
required_representations: Identity of all related parties and description of relationships
Completeness of disclosures about related parties
Appropriate accounting for and disclosure of related party transactions
All transactions with related parties have been disclosed to auditor
management_representations.exam_note: Management representation letter must address related parties

fraud_considerations.related_parties_as_fraud_risk: Related party transactions are specifically identified as fraud risk factor

fictitious_revenue.scheme: Record sales to related parties who don't actually pay or take possession
fictitious_revenue.detection: Confirm with related party, examine subsequent collection, inspect shipping documents

round_trip_transactions.scheme: Company and related party engage in offsetting transactions to create appearance of revenue/activity
round_trip_transactions.purpose: Inflate revenue, create appearance of business activity
round_trip_transactions.detection: Look for circular flows, transactions that net to zero, lack of economic substance

concealing_related_party_nature.scheme: Intentionally conceal that counterparty is related party
concealing_related_party_nature.purpose: Hide that transaction is not at arm's length
concealing_related_party_nature.detection: Finding undisclosed related party is major red flag

shifting_income.scheme: Shift income to/from related entities to achieve desired tax or earnings result
shifting_income.detection: Evaluate business rationale, assess whether terms are reasonable

fraud_considerations.heightened_skepticism: Apply heightened professional skepticism to related party transactions, particularly if:

tip_1_identification_primarily_inquiry.description: Primary method for identifying related parties is INQUIRY with management
tip_1_identification_primarily_inquiry.also: Review records (stockholder lists, board minutes, contracts)
tip_1_identification_primarily_inquiry.exam_question: How does auditor identify related parties? Answer: Inquire with management (primary method)

tip_2_business_rationale_critical.description: Must evaluate business rationale for significant related party transactions
tip_2_business_rationale_critical.red_flag: No clear business purpose = possible fraud or earnings management
tip_2_business_rationale_critical.exam_scenario: Question describes transaction with no apparent purpose - auditor should question economic substance

tip_3_disclosure_requirements.must_disclose: Nature of relationship, description, amounts, terms

tip_4_fraud_risk.common_schemes: Fictitious revenue, round-trip transactions, concealing relationship
tip_4_fraud_risk.finding_undisclosed: Major red flag - reconsider risk assessment and management reliability

tip_5_management_override_connection.description: Significant unusual transactions (often related party) must be evaluated per management override procedures
tip_5_management_override_connection.required: Understand business rationale, evaluate complexity, assess accounting
tip_5_management_override_connection.exam_link: Ties to fraud procedures for management override

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: How does auditor identify related parties?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Inquire with management (primary), review records, be alert during audit

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What disclosures required for related parties?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Nature, description, amounts, terms per ASC 850

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Auditor discovers previously undisclosed related party - what to do?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Inquire why not disclosed, look for other undisclosed parties/transactions, reconsider risk assessment

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Transaction has no apparent business purpose - implications?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Red flag - may lack economic substance, possible fraud, apply skepticism

memorization_aids.fraud_risk: Related parties = Related to fraud risk

key_concepts: Related party = control or significant influence relationship
Transactions may not be arm's length - present audit and fraud risk
Primary identification method: INQUIRY with management
Must evaluate business rationale for significant transactions
Required disclosures: nature, description, amounts, terms (ASC 850)
Cannot claim arm's length unless substantiated
Management representations required about related parties
Finding undisclosed related party = major red flag
Related party transactions specifically identified as fraud risk
critical_for_exam: Cannot claim arm's length without evidence
common_mistakes: Thinking economic dependence alone makes parties related (need control/influence)
Not recognizing inquiry as primary identification method
Not evaluating business rationale for transactions
Allowing FS to claim arm's length without substantiation
Not recognizing undisclosed related party as major red flag

primary_standards: AU-C Section 240: Fraud (related parties as risk factor)

related_topics: fraud_risk_assessment - related parties are fraud risk factor
audit_evidence - evaluating evidence about related party transactions
